entry.title: How much does an AI agent cost: what shapes the price
entry.summary:
Before answering how much an AI agent costs to develop, you need to understand how it differs from an ordinary GPT chat. The price depends on the functions you want it to have An AI agent is a system running on your remote server or your computer. It has its own memory and working tools, and it can run around the clock In an ordinary chat, you ask a question and get a response. A separate agent can keep working while the app on your phone is closed. To do that, it needs connected tools and configured tasks it can carry out without your involvement That makes developing an agent a little more involved than talking to an AI in an app. The system needs to be set up for a particular job: what it remembers, which tools it uses and which services it connects to

entry.title: Privacy Budgets for Test Email in Web Apps
entry.summary: Email is often treated as harmless test plumbing. In a web application, it is closer to a small data store: messages can contain personal-looking addresses, sign-in links, verification codes, and enough context to explain what a user did. When a test fails, that data may then be copied into CI logs, screenshots, artifacts, or a developer's laptop. A useful pattern is to give test email a privacy budget. The budget is not a single number. It is a set of limits for who owns a fixture, how long it lives, what evidence may be retained, and which parts of a message can be exposed to a test. This makes Privacy a design property of Web Development, rather than a cleanup task at the end. Browser and API tests need realistic signals. entry.title: Properties Without Witnesses Are Decorations: A Falsifiability Gate for Agent Patches
entry.summary:
A property that passes on the patched tree and on the pre-patch tree carries no information. That is the first thing to measure, before you trust any property an agent wrote for you. Most agent-written property tests fail this way. The agent reads the diff, writes an invariant that the new code obviously satisfies, and the suite goes green in both trees. The test is not wrong. It is simply unable to distinguish the two states, which makes it a decoration, not a check. This post describes a gate with three rules and one artifact. Properties need a committed witness and a measured detection rate on the baseline. Fixtures must be isolated per sample, verified by transcript hashing. Flaky-frozen tests are forbidden from acting as oracles. The gate is small enough to run on every agent patch.
